assessment: Single-pair survival with a memeco on a memeco spread, plus a rejection pattern dominated by split-half cointegration failures (7 of 14 rejections), signals a market where short-horizon equilibrium relationships between tokens are unstable rather than absent. The fact that hedge ratios and cointegration themselves don't survive a split-half test on most candidates is more consistent with structural drift and regime churn than with elevated dislocations — i.e., not enough shared stationary dynamics for the pipeline to certify a cointegrated residual. The lone survivor is a same-sector, highly correlated pair, which is the type of relationship most likely to remain stationary when cross-asset links are weakening.
opportunity_set: One tradeable pair: 1000SHIB/DOGE. The economic rationale is straightforward — both are dog-themed meme tokens with overlapping holder bases, similar liquidity venues, and tightly correlated flows, so their relative value should mean-revert. The evidence supports this: strong ADF rejection of a unit root (p=0.0004), Hurst of 0.40 indicating genuine anti-persistence rather than a trending residual, a usable 19-hour half-life, a reasonable positive beta of +0.71, and 64 mean crossings giving the cost-aware OU bands enough round trips to be profitable. This is a defensible single-pair book, not a marginal call.
risks: Concentration risk is the dominant concern: the entire book rests on one pair in one sector (memecoins), so a memecoin-specific event — a narrative rotation, a large SHIB or DOGE unlock/rug, or a venue-level funding/liquidity shock on either perp leg — hits the portfolio with full force. Secondary risks: (1) the 19h half-life is toward the slower end of the usable band, so the pair will sit through meaningful drawdowns before mean-reversion pays off and is sensitive to OU parameter drift if the DOGE/SHIB regime shifts; (2) beta of 0.71 means the residual is meaningfully exposed to absolute DOGE moves even when the spread is well-positioned; (3) costs on these high-tick, low-unit-price names can be larger than they appear, and the 64-crossing density floor was the gate that kept this pair honest — if crossings decay, the bands need to widen, not the threshold loosened.
adaptation: Universe has shrunk to a single pair from a previously active SHIB/DOGE position — the pair name is the same on both sides of the refit, so this is a continuation rather than a substitution, but the surrounding candidate set has thinned considerably versus the previous refit (where the same pair was active alongside others). The qualitative shift is toward a memecoin-relative-value regime: cross-sector cointegration candidates are failing split-half stability, while the tight same-sector meme pair is the only relationship currently stable enough to pass. The agent should treat this as a reduced-conviction, single-pair book and size accordingly, rather than assume the prior diversification carries forward.

assessment: An empty selection day signals a market regime where structural relationships between assets have broken down or become unstable rather than merely being mispriced. The rejection pattern is dominated by instability rather than weak cointegration per se: five pairs fail split-half cointegration, one more fails solely on hedge-ratio instability, and five fail the half-life band, meaning where a long-run equilibrium was detectable it was not mean-reverting on a tradable timescale. Combined with two mean-crossing-density failures and one Hurst that was not anti-persistent, the picture is of a regime in which apparent correlations are regime-dependent or trending rather than stationary. The single FDR rejection is the least informative signal of stress because the Benjamini-Hochberg correction only fires when many candidates look marginally cointegrated; the dominant failures here are temporal stability filters, which is a different and arguably more dangerous kind of risk — false confidence has not been manufactured, but genuine mean-reversion is currently absent.
opportunity_set: There is no tradeable set today, and the agent should not relax any threshold to create one. The held pair (SHIB/DOGE) was inherited from a previous refit and was not reconfirmed by the current selection; in this regime its continued presence should be treated with particular caution because the very filters that protect against stale or regime-shifted cointegration were unable to revalidate the relationship today. Holding it is not necessarily wrong — exit bands are calibrated to OU first-passage times and may still be intact — but the absence of fresh statistical confirmation means there is no active edge from this refit, only the residual position and its existing stops.
risks: The dominant risk is regime change in the SHIB/DOGE relationship itself: if memecoin correlation has shifted from stationary to trending or to a different equilibrium, the mean-reversion assumption underpinning the open pair is the exact property today's rejections are flagging as absent across the broader candidate set. With no new pairs entering to diversify or replace, the agent carries concentrated, unconfirmed exposure in a single cointegrated relationship inside a market that is broadly failing stability tests — a textbook setup where a previously valid trade becomes a directional bet without the agent noticing the transition.
adaptation: The universe has effectively contracted to a single legacy position; today's refit did not add any pair and could not revalidate the surviving one. Versus the previous refit, the agent's active book has not shrunk in count but has lost statistical freshness, so the meaningful shift is qualitative rather than quantitative: opportunity has migrated from a diversified multi-pair mean-reversion book toward a single unconfirmed holding, and the adaptation is to do nothing on the selection side and instead let the OU-based exit bands manage the inherited trade until a future refit either reconfirms SHIB/DOGE or exits it on its own.

assessment: The market currently supports only a single statistically defensible cointegration relationship, and it is a high-beta intra-meme-coin spread. The bulk of today's rejections were structural rather than regime-driven: four pairs failed split-half cointegration (the relationship didn't hold up across subsamples), three had half-lives outside the band (either too fast or too slow for tradeable reversion), three failed the Hurst anti-persistence cap (trending rather than mean-reverting), and three fell below the mean-crossing density floor. Only one pair was rejected purely on FDR grounds, which means the issue is not a regime where many spurious correlations look cointegrated — it is a regime where genuine cointegration itself is scarce. This points to a market where most asset pairs are either trending independently or have unstable long-run linkages, consistent with a sentiment-driven, factor-rotating crypto environment rather than a stable beta-driven one.
opportunity_set: A single pair, SHIB/DOGE with a positive beta near 0.79, short half-life around 12 hours, Hurst well inside the anti-persistent zone at 0.37, ADF p-value firmly rejecting a unit root at 0.0001, and 84 mean crossings indicating a richly oscillating spread. Economically, SHIB and DOGE are both retail-meme, attention-driven assets whose prices are driven by overlapping flows of speculative capital, social-media narrative cycles, and exchange-driven liquidity; their relative-value spread should revert when the meme rotation overheats one versus the other. The fast half-life, deep anti-persistence, and dense mean crossings together indicate this spread oscillates frequently and predictably, giving the OU first-passage bands enough crossings to actually trigger entries and exits rather than sit in dead money. With no previous pair to compare against, today's tradeable set is narrow but the one candidate looks high-quality on every gate.
risks: Concentration risk dominates: the entire book rests on one pair whose two legs are highly correlated in narrative, liquidity, and holder base. A broad meme-sector delisting event, exchange withdrawal shock, or shift in retail attention away from both tokens simultaneously would break the cointegration not because of parameter drift but because the shared economic driver disappears. Additionally, both legs are low-liquidity relative to majors, so cost-aware bands may compress sharply and slippage around the OU entry/exit thresholds could erode the edge implied by the statistical gates. There is no diversification benefit across pairs to absorb a regime change.
adaptation: This is the agent's first refit, so there is no prior universe to shift from; the universe has initialized to a single meme-pair inside the SHIB/DOGE cluster and contains nothing from major-vs-major, layer-1, DeFi, or stablecoin-anchored pairs. Going forward, the comparison baseline is now set: any future refit that retains only meme-internal spreads, or that fails to surface any cross-sector (e.g., major-vs-alt or DeFi-vs-layer-1) cointegration, would indicate the regime has become more narrative-driven and less anchored by fundamental liquidity flows, and the agent should be watched for overfitting to a narrow behavioral factor.

assessment: The market is showing a strongly regime-specific opportunity: meme-coin pair dynamics within the same sub-sector (large-cap dog vs. small-cap dog) are exhibiting the kind of high-frequency mean-reversion the pipeline is built to detect, while the broader market has lost the cross-asset cointegration that previously anchored the book (BTC/ETH specifically did not survive). The Hurst of 0.34 confirms genuine anti-persistence rather than a trending pair that merely looks stationary, and the 14-hour half-life indicates the disequilibrium decays quickly enough to fund round-trip costs. The rejection pattern is informative: six pairs failed the mean-crossing density floor and four failed split-half cointegration, which together suggest that most candidate spreads are either drifting or structurally unstable rather than trending, consistent with a market where idiosyncratic shocks dominate over common-factor moves. The three Hurst failures indicate some pairs that look cointegrated in sample are actually trending reversals, and the single FDR rejection is a healthy sign that false-discovery control is not the binding constraint.
opportunity_set: The book collapses to a single, narrow, sector-concentrated trade: 1000SHIB/DOGE. The economic rationale is concrete and defensible — both legs are dog-themed meme tokens that share a common narrative and retail-flow driver, so their relative valuation tends to mean-revert even when absolute prices are volatile. The high mean-crossing count (81) over the lookback, sub-0.5 Hurst, sub-15-hour half-life, and stable hedge ratio of +0.85 all support frequent, fast-decaying entries. However, this is a single-pair book with no diversification across sectors or factor exposures — the opportunity set is honest but thin, and reflects that genuine statistical arbitrage opportunities today exist in only one micro-structure niche.
risks: Concentration risk is dominant on three dimensions simultaneously. First, single-pair concentration: one failed trade has a large expected impact on book P&L. Second, sector concentration: both legs are meme-token narratives correlated to retail sentiment, so a sentiment shock hits both legs at once and the hedge collapses just when it is most needed. Third, the previous BTC/ETH anchor — which provided a slower, large-cap, liquidity-rich counterweight — is gone, removing the diversifying exposure that previously cushioned meme-coin drawdowns. Liquidity risk in 1000SHIB specifically is non-trivial: spreads and slippage on the by-quote leg can widen sharply during stress, and cost-aware OU entry bands calibrated to normal liquidity may be too tight in a dislocation. Finally, mean-reversion in meme spreads is notoriously regime-dependent and can disappear abruptly when a narrative shift drives one leg persistently.
adaptation: The universe has shifted from a two-pair, cross-sector book (a large-cap crypto-relative pair BTC/ETH plus a meme pair) to a one-pair, single-sector book concentrated entirely in dog-themed meme tokens. The agent has lost its cross-asset diversification anchor and is now fully exposed to one sub-niche of crypto. This is not a loosening of standards — the surviving pair genuinely clears every gate — but it is a meaningful structural contraction in opportunity. Operationally, position sizing on 1000SHIB/DOGE should reflect that it now carries the entire book's risk budget, and entry thresholds should be re-checked against 1000SHIB-specific liquidity rather than the previous mix. The next refit should watch for either (a) BTC/ETH-style cross-asset cointegration re-emerging as a regime change, or (b) additional meme-sector pairs (e.g., other large-vs-small dog-themed combinations) qualifying, which would restore some sector-internal diversification.

assessment: Today's selection is very thin — only one pair cleared every statistical screen, indicating a market regime in which genuine, stable cointegration is scarce. The Engle-Granger result survives the BH-FDR filter, the cointegration and hedge ratio are stable across split halves, the Hurst sits at 0.45 (clearly anti-persistent), the half-life of 25h sits inside the tradeable band, and the mean-crossing count comfortably exceeds the floor. The rejection pattern itself is informative: the largest bucket is split-half cointegration instability (price 10 versus 11 entries that passed point-in-time tests but did not survive half-sample re-estimation), followed by too-few mean-crossings (price 6 entries that lack the oscillation density required for cost-aware band harvesting). Smaller counts of Hurst failures (price 2), FDR rejections (price 1) and beta-out-of-range (price 1) are consistent with a market where most candidate spreads are either trending within samples or not mean-reverting tightly enough. The previously active meme-coin leg-pair (SHIB/DOGE perp) likely fell out because the SHIB leg's volatility regime changed enough that the hedge ratio became unstable across split halves — a classic failure mode for high-beta, sentiment-driven pairs during regime shifts.
opportunity_set: A one-pair book is honest about the regime but operationally fragile. ALGO/HBAR is the only pair the statistical machinery currently certifies as cointegrated, with a unit-root-respecting ADF p-value, a hedge ratio essentially at parity (+0.98), a sub-day-capable 25-hour half-life inside the OU banding window, and 41 mean crossings giving enough oscillation density for the first-passage-time entry/exit bands to generate signals at non-trivial frequency. The economic rationale: ALGO and HBAR are both proof-of-stake Layer-1 smart-contract networks competing in a similar addressable market, with overlapping validator/developer ecosystems and similar sensitivity to the same macro risk-on/off and ETH-beta factor — so a stationary spread between them is interpretable as relative-funding-and-narrative flows rather than a spurious statistical artifact. That said, a single-pair book is insufficient for diversification: any idiosyncratic event in either name (token unlock, governance event, exchange incident, listing/delist) will dominate the agent's P&L.
risks: Concentration risk on a single pair, plus correlated-factor risk within that pair. The same thematic overlap that makes ALGO/HARB cointegrated also means a broad L1-sector deleveraging or a shift in the relative-valuation narrative between staking L1s would break the spread exactly when it matters most. The 25-hour half-life is borderline — if realized mean-reversion slows even modestly, the OU first-passage bands will widen and realized round-trip slippage on a thin alt-L1 pair could erode edge. There is no second pair to absorb either a stop or a regime break.
adaptation: The agent's universe has contracted sharply from the previous refit. The prior active book centered on a high-beta meme-coin perp pair (SHIB/DOGE), which is the kind of candidate that typically gets admitted under loose screens but fails the stricter stability and anti-persistence gates the moment volatility falls or one leg's drift regime changes; that pair has now been rejected, almost certainly on split-half cointegration and/or mean-crossing density given the rejection mix. Today's surviving set has migrated to a fundamentally different sleeve — large-cap staking L1 altcoins rather than high-beta memecoin perps — implying the market has shifted from a momentum/sentiment-driven regime where correlated-meme spreads oscillated quickly into a calmer, factor-driven regime where only the most fundamentally-linked L1 pairs maintain a stationary spread. The agent should not loosen any threshold to refill the book; it should accept the thin selection, size ALGO/HBAR conservatively, and wait for the regime to broaden before adding exposure.

assessment: A sparse selection day: the candidate universe tested produced only one pair that survived every gate, indicating a market regime that has thinned out tradeable mean-reverting structures rather than a healthy field of opportunities. The rejection pattern is informative — six pairs failed split-half cointegration (the dominant failure mode) and four were killed by Hurst being too high, meaning the universe contains plenty of nominally-stationary spreads but almost none that are both cointegrated on independent halves and anti-persistent enough to be safely mean-reverting. Three mean-crossing failures add to a regime picture of slow-drifting, trending residual processes rather than oscillating ones. The previously active perp pair (ALGO/USDT vs HBAR/USDT) is no longer in the tradeable set, which is consistent with this thinning-out read rather than with a sudden broadening of opportunities.
opportunity_set: A single survivor: 1000SHIB/DOGE, with strong fundamentals — ADF p=0.0060 is comfortably significant, Hurst of 0.37 sits in the sweet spot for OU-like mean reversion, half-life of 15h is operationally workable for a daily-refit systematic, beta of 0.88 is a clean near-1 hedge on two highly correlated memecoin/canine tokens, and 53 mean crossings over the sample indicates the spread genuinely oscillates rather than drifts. Economically it is the most defensible single survivor one could ask for in this corner of crypto: two assets with overlapping retail flows, shared narrative exposure, and a beta near unity means the pair captures memecoin beta on both legs and isolates a thin relative-value component. With only one pair, the agent's capacity to express its view is sharply reduced and diversification across the tradeable set is essentially zero.
risks: Concentration / opportunity-set starvation: with a single pair and a previously-running position closed, the agent is one bad day away from having nothing to trade at all. Beyond set-size risk, this single survivor carries idiosyncratic memecoin-cluster risk — both legs are highly correlated memecoins, so the 'hedge' is largely against the same factor, and any memecoin-sector blowup will move the spread jointly with the broader market. The 15h half-life combined with crypto's gap-rate volatility during weekends and off-hours also means execution slippage can be a meaningful share of the expected edge on a single trade.
adaptation: Universe has narrowed sharply versus the previous refit: the previously active ALGO/HBAR/USDT perp pair is no longer present and only one new pair emerged from the full candidate scan, so the tradeable set has effectively turned over with a net loss of one. No loosening of thresholds was applied — the absence of candidates reflects the regime, not the gates — but the agent should be aware that its realized trade frequency will drop until either memecoin dispersion rises again or a new cointegrating structure forms in the perp or majors universe.

assessment: The market is offering a narrow but high-quality cointegration opportunity set dominated by two structurally different pair archetypes: a gold-token pair (PAXG/XAUT) and a memecoin pair (1000SHIB/DOGE). The rejection pattern is informative: the most common failures are too few mean crossings (3) and half-life out of band (3), followed by Hurst too high (2) and split-half cointegration failures (2). This distribution is characteristic of a regime where many candidate pairs exhibit trending rather than mean-reverting behavior — the Hurst rejections and the high half-life rejections together point to persistence and slow reversion dominating the candidate pool. Only one pair failed FDR correction and one failed the hedge-ratio stability test, so the statistical gates themselves are doing their job; the bottleneck is genuine mean-reversion quality, not filter stringency.
opportunity_set: The two survivors are both economically defensible but for very different reasons. PAXG/XAUT passes with an exceptionally strong profile: near-perfect beta (+0.96), deep anti-persistence (Hurst 0.25), fast half-life of 9 hours, and 97 mean crossings — this is essentially a same-asset pair (two representations of gold) trading a small but exploitable issuance/redemption and venue basis, which is a structural arbitrage rather than a statistical one. 1000SHIB/DOGE is the more interesting statistical trade: lower beta (+0.84), higher Hurst (0.43, still in mean-reverting territory), a slower 17-hour half-life, and 89 mean crossings. Its economic rationale is shared retail-flow and narrative exposure within the memecoin complex, where liquidity rotations between large- and small-cap memecoins produce a stationary spread. Both pairs survived split-half cointegration and hedge-ratio stability, so the recent and prior halves of the sample agree the relationship is real.
risks: The dominant risk is concentration: the entire tradeable set is two pairs, and the two are highly uncorrelated to each other in both asset class and microstructure (physical-backed gold tokens vs. memecoins), so the portfolio is not diversified in any meaningful sense — a single adverse regime shift hits one pair hard with no offset. Within PAXG/XAUT the risk is that the small mispricing band may be competed away by authorized participants and the residual opportunity set could be near-zero net of costs; a few basis points of slippage on a 9-hour half-life can erase the edge. For 1000SHIB/DOGE the risk is the 17-hour half-life combined with memecoin tail risk — a narrative shock to either token can produce a slow, costly divergence that the mean reversion cannot outpace, and the higher Hurst (0.43) means the spread is closer to a random walk than the gold pair.
adaptation: Relative to the previous refit, the universe has contracted but the surviving pairs are the same two names that were previously active, so the agent is in a continuity regime rather than a rotation: no new pair discoveries, no removals, just a re-confirmation that PAXG/XAUT and 1000SHIB/DOGE remain the only cointegration-grade opportunities in the candidate pool. The continuity is itself a signal — the rejection mix (especially the Hurst and half-life failures) suggests the broader market is in a less mean-reverting state than the survivors, so the agent should treat these two pairs as a high-conviction but thin book and avoid expanding exposure beyond the statistical gates to chase activity.

assessment: The surviving set indicates a highly selective, bifurcated regime. PAXG/XAUT reflects a strong, fast mean-reverting gold-token relationship, while ALGO/HBAR shows a weaker but still statistically admissible altcoin relationship. The 13 rejections—dominated by insufficient mean crossings, followed by unstable cointegration—suggest that broad pairwise convergence is not dependable in the current market. The other failures in half-life and Hurst indicate that several nominally trending or persistent relationships lack the required mean-reversion characteristics.
opportunity_set: The tradeable set is narrow and economically driven. PAXG/XAUT is the stronger opportunity: both represent claims on gold exposure, which provides a plausible common-factor basis, and the +0.96 hedge ratio, 7-hour half-life, and 131 crossings support a tight, liquid mean-reverting structure. ALGO/HBAR is less clearly fundamental but qualifies on all required tests, with a +0.73 hedge ratio, 36-hour half-life, and 31 crossings; its rationale is convergence between two large-cap, DeFi- and payments-adjacent crypto assets rather than an explicit shared fundamental anchor. Its 0.0509 ADF result is also less decisive than PAXG/XAUT's, so it should be treated as the more fragile member of the set.
risks: The principal risk is regime dependence in a very small opportunity set. PAXG/XAUT should remain comparatively robust because its tokens share gold exposure, but token-specific premiums, redemptions, custody, and venue basis can disrupt the underlying relationship. ALGO/HBAR carries greater idiosyncratic, beta, liquidity, and structural-break risk because its economic linkage is less direct and its statistical evidence is marginal. Fast reversion can also amplify execution slippage, while the limited number of crossings in ALGO/HBAR makes band-based signals less well supported. Costs may erode the advantage if spreads, fees, funding, and slippage rise.
adaptation: The previously active PAXG/XAUT pair remains active after passing every gate, so the core gold-token opportunity has persisted rather than materially rotating. The universe has broadened by adding ALGO/HBAR as a new altcoin mean-reverting candidate, but it has not become broadly diversified: 13 candidates were rejected, and the dominant reasons point to weak convergence and unstable cointegration. The adaptation is therefore one additional, weaker opportunity alongside the established PAXG/XAUT pair, not a wholesale expansion of the tradeable universe.
